# DESCRIPTION

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to the field of cancer therapy, specifically to the development of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) for the treatment of breast cancer. More particularly, the invention provides anti-prolactin receptor (anti-PRLR) antibodies and ADCs comprising these antibodies, which are effective in targeting and killing PRLR-expressing cancer cells.

## BACKGROUND

Breast cancer is a heterogeneous disease characterized by various subtypes based on the expression of receptor tyrosine kinase HER2 and hormone receptors for estrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR). Approximately 15% to 20% of breast cancers do not express significant levels of these receptors and are classified as triple-negative cancers. These tumors, as well as those that progress following hormonal or HER2 therapies, highlight the need for the development of additional targeted therapeutics in advanced breast cancers.

Prolactin (PRL) is a polypeptide hormone that binds to the prolactin receptor (PRLR), a single-pass transmembrane receptor of the type 1 cytokine receptor superfamily. PRLR signals through multiple intracellular kinases, such as Jak2/Stat5, MAPK, and PI3K. PRLR is overexpressed in malignant breast epithelium and across molecular subtypes of human breast cancers. PRL can increase the proliferation of human breast and prostate cancer cells, suggesting a role for the PRL/PRLR signaling axis in tumor development. However, the contribution of PRLR signaling in advanced breast cancer remains contentious.

Several strategies have been employed to target PRLR in cancer, including PRL-based antagonists and antibodies. However, the clinical utility of these antagonists has been limited due to issues such as short serum half-life, immunogenicity, and toxicity. Antibodies to PRLR, such as LFA-102 and 005-C04, have demonstrated the ability to inhibit PRL-mediated signaling in vitro and in vivo, but their antitumor efficacy has been weak.

Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have proven useful for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer due to the selective delivery of highly potent cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. The anti-HER2 ADC Kadcyla (adotrastuzumab emtansine) is approved for the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer. The present invention provides a novel anti-PRLR ADC, REGN2878-DM1, which demonstrates potent in vitro cytotoxicity and antitumor activity in several breast cancer xenograft models.

## BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides anti-PRLR antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) comprising these antibodies. The ADCs are effective in targeting and killing PRLR-expressing cancer cells, particularly in breast cancer. The invention includes methods for generating and characterizing the anti-PRLR antibodies and ADCs, as well as their use in treating breast cancer.

The anti-PRLR antibodies and ADCs of the invention exhibit high affinity for human PRLR and effectively block PRL-mediated signaling. The ADCs, specifically REGN2878-DM1, are internalized by PRLR-expressing cells and trafficked to lysosomes, where the cytotoxic drug is released and induces cell death. The invention also provides methods for assessing the expression of PRLR in breast cancer samples and for evaluating the antitumor activity of the ADCs in vitro and in vivo.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Definitions

As used herein, the term "antibody" refers to an immunoglobulin molecule that is capable of specifically binding to a target, such as a protein or a peptide. The term encompasses intact immunoglobulin molecules, as well as fragments thereof, such as Fab, F(ab')2, and Fv fragments, that retain the ability to bind to the target.

The term "antibody-drug conjugate" (ADC) refers to a complex comprising an antibody covalently linked to a cytotoxic drug. The ADC is designed to deliver the cytotoxic drug specifically to cells expressing the target antigen, thereby minimizing toxicity to non-target cells.

The term "prolactin receptor" (PRLR) refers to a single-pass transmembrane receptor of the type 1 cytokine receptor superfamily. PRLR is involved in the signaling pathway mediated by prolactin (PRL) and is overexpressed in various types of cancer, including breast cancer.

The term "internalization" refers to the process by which a cell takes up an extracellular molecule, such as an antibody or an ADC, into its cytoplasm. Internalization can occur through various mechanisms, including receptor-mediated endocytosis.

### Anti-PRLR Antibodies Comprising Fc Variants

The present invention provides anti-PRLR antibodies that exhibit high affinity for human PRLR and effectively block PRL-mediated signaling. The antibodies are generated using VelocImmune mice, which are genetically engineered to produce human antibodies. The antibodies are selected based on their ability to bind to PRLR, internalize into cells, and block PRL-mediated signaling.

The antibodies of the invention can be modified to include Fc variants that enhance their effector functions, such as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). The Fc variants can be introduced by site-directed mutagenesis or other methods known in the art.

### Biological Characteristics of the Antibodies

The anti-PRLR antibodies of the invention exhibit high affinity for human PRLR, with dissociation constants (Kd) in the nanomolar range. The antibodies effectively block the binding of PRL to PRLR and inhibit PRL-mediated signaling, as measured by luciferase reporter assays and other in vitro assays.

The antibodies are internalized by PRLR-expressing cells and trafficked to lysosomes, where they are degraded. This internalization and degradation process is crucial for the delivery of the cytotoxic drug in ADCs.

### Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs)

The present invention provides antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) comprising the anti-PRLR antibodies of the invention. The ADCs are designed to deliver a cytotoxic drug specifically to PRLR-expressing cells, thereby minimizing toxicity to non-target cells.

The ADCs of the invention are prepared by conjugating the anti-PRLR antibodies to a cytotoxic drug, such as DM1, via a non-cleavable SMCC linker. The drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) of the ADCs is typically between 3 and 4, ensuring optimal balance between stability and potency.

### Targeting ADCs to Cells Expressing Low Levels of PRLR

The ADCs of the invention are effective in targeting and killing cells with low-to-moderate levels of PRLR expression, as well as cells with high PRLR expression. This broad range of activity is due to the rapid internalization and lysosomal degradation of the ADCs, which ensures efficient release of the cytotoxic drug.

### Class I Cytokine Receptor Targeting

PRLR belongs to the class I cytokine receptor superfamily, which includes receptors such as the growth hormone receptor. The targeting of class I cytokine receptors with ADCs is a promising strategy for the treatment of various cancers, as these receptors are often overexpressed in tumor cells and play a critical role in tumor development and progression.

### Epitope Mapping and Related Technologies

Epitope mapping is used to identify the specific regions of PRLR that are recognized by the anti-PRLR antibodies of the invention. This information is crucial for optimizing the binding affinity and specificity of the antibodies and for designing ADCs with improved therapeutic properties.

### Preparation of Human Antibodies

The anti-PRLR antibodies of the invention are prepared using VelocImmune mice, which are genetically engineered to produce human antibodies. The antibodies are isolated from hybridomas or directly from antigen-binding splenocytes and cloned into expression vectors for production in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells.

### Bioequivalents

The present invention also encompasses bioequivalent forms of the anti-PRLR antibodies and ADCs, including variants and derivatives that retain the ability to bind to PRLR and inhibit PRL-mediated signaling. These bioequivalents can be produced using various methods known in the art, such as site-directed mutagenesis, chemical modification, and glycosylation engineering.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1. Generation of Anti-PRLR Antibodies

VelocImmune mice were immunized with recombinant human PRLR extracellular domain. Spleens were harvested for generation of hybridomas or for direct isolation of antigen-binding splenocytes. The cloned human immunoglobulin variable region genes from antibodies exhibiting the desired characteristics were joined to human IgG1 constant region genes for production in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. The anti-PRLR monoclonal antibody, herein referred to as REGN2878, was selected as a lead antibody from more than 300 antigen-binding clones following screening by in vitro biochemical and cell-based assays for specificity, affinity, internalization, and blockade of ligand-mediated signaling.
